reasoning: Both round-1 required changes are in the updated diff. (1) Duplication: there is now one copy of the launch, drain and kill logic, in Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Util/BoundedProcess.swift:495-539 (diff lines 495-539). It runs with null stdin and stderr, drains stdout on a background thread, uses a single deadline, sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL, and all of that sits in one place. SecurityToolCredentialReader.runTool (diff 387-448) went from about 50 lines to about 20 and delegates to it. That reader keeps its race-window acceptance as its own logic through `outcome.exitedCleanly`, so it behaves the same: `exitedCleanly` requires `drained`, which matches the old `drainedInTime` check. TeamSignatureDMGVerifier.runHdiutil (DMGVerifier.swift:164-174) is now 10 lines of mapping only. (2) Error naming: Failure now has separate cases, `launchFailed(String)`, `timedOut`, `hdiutilExited(Int32)` (which keeps the exit status) and `indirect detachFailed(Failure)`. `mountFailed` is now used only where the attach plist has no mount point (DMGVerifier.swift:160). The detach log wraps the real cause (DMGVerifier.swift:126-132). The new helper's API is reasonable. It is a caseless `enum` namespace. `Outcome: Sendable` is a value type that carries only facts. `terminationReason` is nil while the child is still running, which avoids reading `Process.terminationReason` on a live process (that raises an exception). `exitedCleanly` is named for exactly what it checks. The doc comment says the call blocks for up to timeout + ~3 s and that callers must keep it off the cooperative pool. The DMG verifier follows that by running it in `Task.detached`. `try process.run()` passes its error up instead of swallowing it. The only `try?` in the diff is cleanup of the temp root, which CLAUDE.md allows. There is no new wrapper or ceremony, and the new Core file has tests as CLAUDE.md §4 requires (BoundedProcessTests: happy path, non-zero exit, timeout, SIGKILL after an ignored TERM, launch failure). Those tests use only non-optional `#expect` asserts, which the Bool rule allows. Two small points, neither enough to change the vote. First, `status` is set to a 0 sentinel when `terminationReason == nil`. That is documented, but a caller that forgets to check could misread it as a clean exit. Second, `hdiutilExited` also carries the signal number when hdiutil dies from a signal. I did not build this, as instructed, so I have not measured warnings. `Outcome: Sendable` holding `Process.TerminationReason`, an imported ObjC enum, is expected to be Sendable, but that is not confirmed by a compile.
